notes: Summary: Mid-market product team building advanced in-app assistant + search/rerank for product docs and customer support.
Current stack: uses incumbent LLM API (OpenAI) for embeddings and chat; exploring migration to Redwood Hosted for cost predictability then Dedicated for production SLA.
Primary drivers: lower per-token unit economics at scale, predictable latency, stronger VPC options for customer data, better rollout controls (canary/A-B).

POC scope: 1) API parity layer to emulate incumbent endpoints, 2) prompt parity validation (system msg handling, tokenization), 3) embeddings drift checks across datasets, 4) rerank pipeline throughput tests.
Latency/throughput targets: p95 chat latency <= 250ms for typical queries (<=512 tokens), reranking pipeline ~50 QPS batching window, embeddings batch throughput ~200 docs/s per host.
Cost sensitivity: moderate-high. Target ARR-based threshold where Redwood Dedicated becomes cost-advantageous for embeddings-heavy workloads (~$150k+/yr).
Model preferences: willing to run open and quantized models (Llama2-style) if output quality matches incumbent; want Redwood's model catalog + verified perf profiles.
Security/compliance: SSO/SAML required, SOC2 audited vendor required, audit logs and KMS integration mandatory; legal requested explicit KMS SLA addendum.

Migration notes: experiments show two small regressions in prompt parity vs incumbent: 1) system message normalization changed token offsets for a few templates, 2) embedding cosine drift ~2.8% on product taxonomy causing rerank reorder for edge cases.
Workarounds tried: token-prefix normalization shim in client, normalization retrain for embeddings; both acceptable short-term but want platform-level fixes or guidance (Optimize suggestions).

Operational needs: rollout policy that routes 10% traffic to Redwood Hosted, 90% to incumbent during POC; for Dedicated want canary then full cutover with automatic fallback to Hosted provider if latency spikes.
